SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.21
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is typical of a simple aliphatic dialkyl ether (no O–H or N–H stretch above 3100 cm⁻¹).  Four strong C–H stretches appear at 2784-2952 cm⁻¹, consistent with multiple CH₃ / CH₂ groups.  A prominent band at 1045 cm⁻¹ matches the intense ν(C–O–C) stretch found in alkyl ethers, and the 1158 cm⁻¹ band fits the higher-frequency asymmetric C–O–C stretch of dialkyl ethers (rule GFQ-003).  Bands at 860–880 cm⁻¹ and 779 cm⁻¹ are typical of C–O–C and –CH₂– rocking modes in ethers, while 1469 cm⁻¹ is the CH₃ deformation (GFQ-003).  Among the candidates, compound 4 (CCOCCC(C)OC) is the only purely dialkyl ether with two different alkoxy groups (ethyl and methoxy), giving the required strong ether C–O–C modes and multiple CH₃ groups without any O–H or N–H stretches that are absent experimentally.
